data.title: Staff Backend Engineer
data.description: 🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone. We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking. After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts , accounts for 16-17 year olds , a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save , invest and combine their pensions with us. With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers! We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️ 📍London / UK Remote | 💰 Staff Backend Engineer (L60) £130,000 - £170,000 + Equity + Benefits | Technology - Engineering About our Engineering Teams: We have around 650 engineers out of roughly 5,500 people in total - and we have big ambitions. There are many interesting challenges ahead, and we're happy for people to move between teams or to specialise, whatever you prefer. As an engineer here you'd be able to work directly with anyone across the company, and we run regular knowledge-sharing sessions so you’ll learn heaps about everything from how banks work to effective communication. We contribute to open source software as much as possible. Our blog is a good place to learn even more about what we do! What you’ll be working on: We rely heavily on the following tools and technologies: Go to write our application code (there’s an excellent interactive Go tutorial here ) Cassandra for most persistent data storage Kafka for our asynchronous message queue Envoy Proxy for RPC Kubernetes and Docker to schedule and run our services AWS for most of our infrastructure React for internal web dashboards We also have two physical datacenter sites with actual cables to connect to various third parties Your day-to-day This role is all about collaborating across disciplines to test hypotheses and make a difference to customers. As a product backend engineer you’ll work in a squad alongside product managers, marketers, user researchers, designers, mobile engineers, web engineers, data analysts, business analysts, writers and more! Together you'll build and support a particular part of Monzo. Our squads belong to our wider collectives (a word we use to describe self-governing business units of ~100 people). Our collectives are doing innovative work, many of which have machine learning and AI at the forefront - from fighting financial crime to building smarter financial tools - and you may have the opportunity to join a collective that gives you direct exposure to this exciting space. Our backend engineers have a variety of different backgrounds. As long as you enjoy learning new things, we’d love to talk to you. We do not ask for formal qualifications or degree requirements for any of our engineering roles. How we work 💻 Locations & Flexible Working: Our main tech hub is in London, but our engineers live everywhere in the UK— from Brighton to the Western Isles. We value meeting in person but we don't have a mandated requirement on office attendance, even if you're nearby. We believe you'll do your best work if you are where you want to be. If you live outside of London and we ask you to come into the office, Monzo will support you with the costs. ✨ Our offices are naturally social, especially Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, which happen to line up with our twice-weekly Monzo lunches & treat Thursdays 🍽️. Teams also schedule time together often for work and play – in or around the office, or online. Set up a work schedule that delivers impact and fits your life: At Monzo, we value connections, flexibility, and wellbeing. We keep our meetings during core hours to stay connected and believe in maintaining work/life balance. You’ll be empowered to manage your work in a way that suits you and your team, giving you the freedom for children drop-offs and pick-ups, walking your dog or adventurous cat, avoiding peak commuting times or gym slots, appointments, or supporting your family in an emergency. 🕒✨ If you prefer to work part-time, we'll make this happen whenever we can - whether this is to help you meet other commitments or strike a great work-life balance. Work the way that works for you with Monzo! 💼 You should apply if: you have strong experience working on the backend of a technology product you want to be involved in building a product that you (and the people you know) use every day you have a product mindset: you care about customer outcomes and you want to make data-informed decisions you’re comfortable working in a team that deals with ambiguity you’re interested in distributed systems and writing resilient software you have some experience with strongly-typed languages (Go, Java, C, Scala etc.). you think you’d enjoy the kind of work we’re doing We're on the look out for L60 Engineers at the moment, you can read more in our Engineering Progression Framework we are also hiring on L40 & L50, our interview process will determine your levelling. The Interview Process: Our interview process involves three main stages: Initial Call Take home task or pair coding exercise Final interview including a system design and a behavioural interview Our average process takes around 2-3 weeks but we will always work around your availability. One of our engineers has written a detailed blog on their experience through this process, for extra details, hints and tips please see here . What’s in it for you: 💰 £130,000 - £170,000 + Equity ✈️We can help you relocate to the UK ✅ We can sponsor visas. 📍This role can be based in our London office or remotely across the UK (with ad hoc meetings in London). ⏰We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, at times that suit you and your team. 📚 Learning budget of £1,000 a year for books, training courses and conferences ➕And much more, see our full list of benefits here We're usually always hiring for Backend Engineers, so there's no closing date for this job. #LI-Remote #LI-HJ1 Equal opportunities for everyone Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo. At Monzo, we’re embracing diversity by fostering an inclusive environment for all people to do the best work of their lives with us. This is integral to our mission of making money work for everyone. You can read more in our blog , 2026 Diversity and Inclusion Report and 2025 Gender Pay Gap Report. We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status. If you have a preferred name, please use it to apply. We don't need full or birth names at application stage 😊 Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

We have big ambitions for the future, and technology plays a big role in creating a bank our customers want, so engineers at Monzo collaborate across disciplines to solve interesting challenges throughout the company. These range from the products our customers use everyday to underlying infrastructure, security, payments and finance, customer operations, financial crime, and data, to name just a few areas. As a bank, there is scope for impact across a huge number of opportunities. We contribute to open source software as much as possible. Our blog is a good place to learn even more about what we do! Your day-to-day This role is all about collaborating with your team to make a difference to your customers. As a backend engineer you’ll work in a squad alongside other disciplines like product managers, marketers, user researchers, designers, mobile engineers, web engineers, data analysts, business analysts, writers and more! Together you'll build and support a particular part of Monzo. Our squads belong to our wider collectives (a word we use to describe self-governing business units of ~100 people). They are: Core Banking, Business Banking, Wealth, Borrowing, Growth, Payments, Platform, Fincrime, Security & Expansion. All of our collectives are doing innovative work, many of which have machine learning and AI at the forefront- from fighting financial crime to building smarter financial tools - and you may have the opportunity to join a collective that gives you direct exposure to this exciting space. They’re all looking for additional Backend Engineers right now, we do a standard interview process across all our collectives and at the end we will find the best match for you based on your skills, experience, preferences and aligning with the business need! Our backend engineers have a variety of different backgrounds. As long as you enjoy learning new things, we’d love to talk to you. We do not ask for formal qualifications or degree requirements for any of our engineering roles. How we work 💻 Our main tech hub is in London, but our engineers live everywhere in the UK— from Brighton to the Western Isles. We value meeting in person but we don't have a mandated requirement on office attendance, even if you're nearby. We believe you'll do your best work if you are where you want to be. If you live outside of London and we ask you to come into the office, Monzo will support you with the costs ✨ Our offices are naturally social, especially Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, which happen to line up with our twice-weekly Monzo lunches & treat Thursdays 🍽️ Teams also schedule time together often for work and play – in or around the office, or online. Set up a work schedule that delivers impact and fits your life: At Monzo, we value connections, flexibility, and wellbeing. We keep our meetings during core hours to stay connected and believe in maintaining work/life balance. You’ll be empowered to manage your work in a way that suits you and your team, giving you the freedom for children drop-offs and pick-ups, walking your dog or adventurous cat, avoiding peak commuting times or gym slots, appointments, or supporting your family in an emergency 🕣✨ If you prefer to work part-time, we'll make this happen whenever we can - whether this is to help you meet other commitments or strike a great work-life balance. data.title: Senior Product Manager
data.description: About Motorway Motorway is the UK's largest online car-selling platform. We connect private sellers directly with over 8,000 dealers nationwide. Our online platform helps sellers achieve great prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want for their dealerships. Founded in 2017, our award-winning, technology-led approach has redefined the experience of selling a car. Motorway is backed by some of the world’s leading technology investors, having raised £143 million in Series C funding. This is a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing scale-up at a crucial phase of growth and help change an industry for the better. About the role We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to join Motorway's Product & Engineering team. Motorway is a UK online car-selling platform connecting private sellers with ~7,500 verified dealers through online auctions. You will own a problem area end to end, in either the seller or the dealer side of the marketplace, and be accountable for the outcomes you deliver. Building is cheaper than it has ever been. The hard part now is choosing the right thing to build. We want PMs with exceptional product sense who find the problems worth solving, back that judgement with evidence, and use the latest technology to solve them in ways that weren't possible a year ago. What you will do Find the problems that matter Identify the highest-impact problem areas by combining quantitative analysis with qualitative research, and explain clearly why they matter more than the alternatives See through the hundreds of good ideas to the few that will move the business and create real value for sellers and dealers Own outcome-based goals and metrics, not feature lists Build with AI, in your work and in our product Use AI to make yourself and your team faster: automate routine PM tasks, analyse data and research quickly, and prototype or vibe code solutions to get customer feedback in days, not weeks Ask how each product could be built differently given what AI makes possible, and bring those ideas to your squad Make your team 2x more effective, not 2x busier Deliver with rigour Lead a cross-functional squad of engineers, designers and data specialists from discovery through launch and measurement Run experiments that produce learning even when they fail, and act on what you learn Make clear trade-offs between customer needs, technical constraints and business priorities Bring people with you Communicate the what, the why and the how clearly, through crisp, data-led documents and conversations Work with the people closest to you (engineering, design, data) and with execs and other business units such as Operations, Customer Support, Sales and Marketing Influence without authority and build alignment on difficult decisions Requirements Proven experience as a product manager, with a track record of shipping products that moved meaningful business metrics, not just delivering features Strong product sense. You can show how you found and prioritised the right problem, and what you chose not to do Comfortable with both qualitative and quantitative evidence: you run user research and also query data, design experiments and interpret results yourself Data-oriented. You use data to understand problems, set goals and measure impact, and can debate approaches with data scientists and analysts AI-forward. You use AI tools regularly in your own work and have hands-on experience prototyping or building with them. You have a point of view on where AI helps and where it doesn't A clear, confident communicator who can work with engineers and analysts day to day and with senior leaders across the business Ability to move between detail and strategy without losing coherence Self-starter with strong ownership, a curious mindset, and the ability to build domain knowledge quickly Experience in marketplaces, consumer products or B2B platforms is helpful but not essential You're excited about changing how people buy and sell cars Benefits We offer a fantastic range of benefits to help you thrive: Hybrid work schedule with 2 days per week in our Central London office, with regular social events, office drinks and free snacks to keep you going Great work-life balance Stock options so you can share in Motorway's growth and future success Pension scheme to plan for your future with our provider NEST Strong commitment to your personal development including budget for books, courses, conferences, etc Opt-in comprehensive health insurance through BUPA including dental care and fitness discounts Cycle to work scheme, save big ££ on a new bike and accessories One paid volunteering day a year for you to use as you wish Generous parental benefits including 6 months full paid maternity leave, 4 weeks paternity leave and workplace nursery scheme... and much more! data.title: Director, Maternal & Reproductive Health
data.description: Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL) is a global health organization that partners locally and globally to create and scale solutions to the world’s deadliest health threats. Millions of people die from preventable health threats. We collaborate to close the gap between proven, life-saving solutions and the people who need them. Since 2017, we’ve worked with governments and other partners in more than 60 countries to save millions of lives. We work toward a future where people live longer, healthier lives, communities flourish, and economies thrive. This is an ambitious vision, and it inspires us and our partners to make progress every day. Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL) works with governments and partners to strengthen and transform primary health care (PHC) to improve health and save lives. Our approach focuses on making PHC more prioritized, proactive and accountable for outcomes, and strengthening how care is organized, delivered, financed and measured. Drawing on expertise across RTSL's portfolio, we bring together solutions in health system resilience and epidemic readiness, digital health and data-driven decision-making, performance measurement and improvement, and sustainable health financing. We apply these capabilities to address priority health challenges, including cardiovascular health, maternal survival and sexual and reproductive health, while strengthening health systems to deliver more equitable, effective and resilient care. Position Purpose The Director, Maternal & Reproductive Health will provide strategic and technical leadership for RTSL's portfolio to reduce preventable maternal deaths and improve sexual and reproductive health outcomes. The role will lead the development and implementation of a multi-country program that strengthens government capabilities to identify and address barriers to quality care, translate data into action, and deliver measurable improvements in health outcomes. The Director will have overall accountability for the strategy, resources, quality, performance, and results of the maternal survival and reproductive health portfolio, leading a multidisciplinary team and working closely with governments, technical partners, and colleagues across RTSL to design, implement and scale evidence-informed approaches. The role requires deep expertise in sexual, reproductive and maternal health, strong program leadership, and the ability to translate technical evidence into practical, sustainable health system improvements. Work Location: 100% Remote with travel as stated. Duration: Full-time employment for a fixed term of 24 months. Core Duties and Responsibilities Strategic Leadership and Portfolio Management Set the strategic direction, priorities and implementation approach for RTSL's maternal survival and reproductive health portfolio, exercising delegated authority to make program investment, resource allocation, and partnership decisions within approved organizational parameters and in alignment with country priorities. Oversee a multi-country portfolio, with accountability for program planning, budget development and management, resource allocation, performance and delivery against strategic objectives. Lead and manage a multidisciplinary team, establishing clear responsibilities and performance expectations, overseeing staffing and talent development, addressing performance and capacity gaps, and building the capabilities needed for sustained program delivery. Technical Leadership and Program Development Provide expert technical leadership across maternal survival and sexual and reproductive health, including maternal death surveillance and response, quality maternal care, family planning, and adolescent pregnancy prevention. Lead the development and adaptation of evidence-informed approaches that connect data-driven learning with targeted improvements in clinical care, service delivery and wider health system capabilities. Guide the design and implementation of country programs, identifying opportunities to strengthen government leadership, institutional capabilities and sustainable approaches to improving health outcomes. Drive innovation and collaboration across RTSL's technical teams, drawing on expertise in PHC delivery, digital health, measurement and financing to address priority health system bottlenecks. Country Engagement and Strategic Partnerships Lead senior-level engagement with Ministries of Health and national partners to identify priorities, shape country strategies and secure government ownership of programs and results. Develop and manage strategic partnerships with donors, multilateral agencies, technical institutions and implementing partners, identifying opportunities for collaboration, investment and program expansion, and representing RTSL in high-level technical and policy discussions. Performance, Learning and Accountability Maintain overall accountability for portfolio performance and results, establishing clear performance expectations and monitoring mechanisms, and using evidence and implementation learning to inform strategic decisions, address delivery challenges, and adapt approaches. Oversee the generation, synthesis and dissemination of evidence and practical learning to inform policy, program improvement and scale-up across countries. Qualifications Education Advanced degree in medicine, public health, sexual and reproductive health, obstetrics and gynecology, or a related field. Experience At least 15 years of relevant global health experience, including substantial technical and leadership experience in sexual, reproductive and maternal health in low- and middle-income countries. Demonstrated experience developing and leading complex, multi-country programs, including strategic planning, budget oversight and accountability for results. Extensive experience engaging senior government officials, donors and international partners, with the ability to build relationships and influence strategic decisions. Skills & Abilities Recognized technical expertise in maternal survival and reproductive health, with a strong understanding of evidence-based interventions, health service delivery and health system strengthening. Proven ability to lead and develop multidisciplinary teams and manage programs across different countries and organizational functions. Strong understanding of data-driven program improvement, implementation challenges and approaches to translating evidence into sustainable results. Excellent strategic thinking, judgement, communication and leadership skills, with the ability to navigate complex political and operational environments. Fluency in English required; proficiency in French desirable. Willingness to travel internationally, approximately 30% during program start-up and up to 25% thereafter. Compensation and Benefits Resolve to Save Lives prides itself on cultivating a supportive, connected remote team doing work that matters. We do everything possible to ensure our employees are connected and set up for success. The salary range for applicants based in the US is $150,000 to $170,000 annually. The exact offer will be determined by various factors, such as the candidate's skills and experience relative to the requirements of the role. For applicants based outside the US , salaries are set according to national labor rates for the international NGO sector. In addition to a competitive salary, Resolve to Save Lives provides a generous package of benefits, including: Health insurance for you and your dependents Contributions toward retirement Paid annual leave and sick leave, in addition to public holidays Two paid, week-long organization-wide breaks at mid-year and end-of-year Professional development and home office setup benefits Up-to-date computer equipment Anticipated Application Deadline: 27 November 2026 ( This position may close earlier if a high volume of applications is received before the stated deadline ) RTSL believes its programs are strengthened when they are developed and supported by individuals with diverse life experiences whose understanding of social and cultural issues can help make our work and workforce more inclusive. We encourage applications from and provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, ancestry, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, marital status, organ donor status, or status as a veteran. data.title: Développeur Python IA
data.description: Développeur Python IA (H/F) Paris/Lille | Secteur Assurance Pourquoi cette opportunité ? Parce que vous participerez à la construction de notre stratégie d’intelligence artificielle, que nous sommes en train de définir. Vous rejoindrez une équipe motivée et talentueuse, dont la mission est d’intégrer l’IA au cœur de nos processus métier. L’objectif est de répondre aux besoins de nos équipes comme à ceux de nos clients, et d’automatiser certaines tâches à faible valeur ajoutée. Éléments clés Concevoir des solutions RAG et agentiques appliquées à des cas d’usage métier concrets. Développer et orchestrer des agents tout en assurant la traçabilité des sources et la maîtrise des hallucinations. Contribuer directement au workflow de paramétrage produit KELIA, avec une validation humaine intégrée aux étapes clés. Participer à la mise en production des assistants, de leur API jusqu’à leur intégration dans l’interface web interne. Ce qu’il faut savoir : Nous recherchons un(e) Développeur Python IA pour rejoindre notre équipe R&D à Paris ou Lille Vous interviendrez sur l’ensemble du cycle de vie des solutions, de la conception jusqu’à la mise en production, en mobilisant différentes approches : modèles de langage (LLM), apprentissage supervisé, clustering et autres techniques de machine Learning. Un volet important de la mission concerne également le paramétrage produit : l’objectif est d’extraire les informations pertinentes des conditions générales, de proposer un paramétrage, de prévoir une validation par un expert à chaque étape et de produire un fichier directement importable dans KELIA. Missions principales : Vous développez en Python des fonctionnalités IA. Ingestion documentaire : extraire le texte et les tableaux des PDF, des pages Confluence, des documents SharePoint et des dépôts GitLab, puis découper, indexer et mettre à jour ces contenus avec des jobs asynchrones. Recherche : recherche hybride (sémantique et mots-clés), filtres par collection et par chemin, reranking, et recherche visuelle sur les pages de documents. data.title: Embedded Linux Engineer (Yocto Specialist)
data.description: About Genesis Genesis is a physical AI lab and full-stack robotics company building general-purpose robots, with teams in Paris and the Bay Area. Our people have built some of the most widely used platforms in robotics research including the open-source Genesis simulator, pioneered generative simulation and led foundation-model work at some of the world's leading AI labs. We own the whole stack: hardware, embedded systems, simulation, data and robot foundation models. The Role Every Genesis robot runs on a custom jetson thor compute board and every piece of software we write: control, perception, learned policies, depends on the Linux image underneath it. We are looking for a senior engineer to own that image end to end: build it, ship it to the robot, keep it updatable, and make it easy for the rest of the team to compile and deploy on top of it. This is an in-house ownership role. You will be the reference for embedded Linux at Genesis, working closely with our embedded, robotics and application-software engineers in Paris and with our hardware partners. The job is to provide a reliable, well maintained and up to date os image, customized to our needs. What You'll Do Build, own and maintain the production Yocto/OpenEmbedded distribution for our robot's custom board: BSP, kernel, device tree, rootfs, toolchain and custom layers. Bring up new hardware on NVIDIA Jetson-class platforms, integrating drivers and peripherals. Including hands-on debugging of components such as Wi-Fi, cameras, audio devices and buses on the physical robot. Own the full image lifecycle: reproducible builds, versioned releases, secure and robust over-the-air (OTA) updates, and long-term maintenance as hardware and software evolve. Deliver a development kit and workflow (SDK, cross-compilation, deployment tooling) so engineers can build and ship their software onto the robot quickly. Integrate GPU and AI-accelerator inference stacks so that our models run efficiently on the robot. Speed up the team's build and CI pipeline for image generation and validation. Builds are long, so caching and automation matter, as well as removing unnecessary dependencies. Document the system and make it approachable, so the image is never again a black box that only one person (or contractor) understands. Your First Three Months Build a custom Yocto image for the robot's custom boards. Flash, boot and validate it on real hardware, working through driver and integration issues on-site. Set up the cross compilation workflow, caching, CI automations to streamline the robotics team work What You'll Bring Passion for your craft and demonstrated excellence in embedded Linux engineering. 5+ years of hands-on embedded Linux experience, including shipping at least one Yocto-based image to production not only a prototype. Proven ownership of an image through its lifecycle: maintenance, release management and remote/OTA updates. Deep experience with Yocto internals: layers, recipes, BitBake, machine and distro configuration, SDK generation. Strong board bring-up and low-level debugging skills: kernel configuration, device trees, drivers, boot chain. Hands-on experience with the NVIDIA Jetson family (JetPack / L4T, meta-tegra) or comparable embedded GPU platforms. Knowledge C++ and Python packaging systems and how to deal with cross-compilation. The ability to explain how your work fits into the wider build, development and deployment system. Exceptional ownership and initiative, with the judgment to choose workable solutions for our current stage over the theoretically ideal one. data.title: Quadrants: Compiler Lead
data.description: What Quadrants is Quadrants is an open-source translation layer that turns ordinary Python into optimized machine code at runtime, across CPU (Arm64, x86) and GPU (AMDGPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan) backends. CUDA is the primary target, with x86 the strong runner-up, especially for real-time simulation. The others drive adoption and support fast prototyping for research. The ambition is explicit: build the best “Python compiler” in the world for physics and performance-critical numerical computing. We are fully committed to it, and we intend to beat leading alternatives like Nvidia Warp, Numba, or Triton. It’s a standalone project with its own roadmap, built in the open. Genesis, our physics simulator, is its first and top-priority user, the source of its hardest workloads and its benchmarks. But Quadrants is general-purpose infrastructure for anyone writing performance-critical numerical Python, not an internal tool that happens to be public. The bet: high-performance code should feel natural to write. Engineers write plain Python in a NumPy or PyTorch style, and Quadrants makes it fast. The role You own Quadrants end to end: the API, the IR and lowering, the optimization passes, the numerical primitives, and the roadmap. Our ultimate objective: engineers write for readability and maintainability, never for performance. They write the version of an algorithm they are most comfortable with, and Quadrants rebuilds it into kernels that run as if an expert had hand-tuned them. Performance is the compiler’s job, not theirs. Getting there is a frontier problem, part research and part engineering, and we intend to define the state of the art on it, relentlessly pushing the limit further. It calls for two things at once: the low-level GPU and compiler skill to make a single kernel optimal, and the ability to keep the whole system coherent as it grows. The core tradeoff is settled: usability comes first. When usability and performance collide, usability wins, unless the cost is severe. We will limit what the system supports to go fast (static shapes and fixed-size allocation baked into kernels, say), but never the convenience of the API itself. Experts who want maximum performance and full control over the generated code get lower-level escape hatches, down to inline assembly, C, or PTX. Your mandate is to build the best open-source Python compiler for physics simulation out there. No limit on what that takes. If it means replacing the entire engine, your call. Either way, you keep Quadrants healthy and unblocking the company in the meantime. What you’ll own API & authoring experience. The surface that physics and numerical-computing engineers write against, and, as an open-source library, the product’s face to the world. Idiomatic, natural to Python users, never a separate language bolted onto Python. Clean decorators, legible constraints, sharp errors, real escape hatches. IR, lowering & backends. A stable IR that lowers to multiple backends, with room to grow and the door kept open for differentiable simulation. Today the computation graph is expressed through Quadrants’ own constructs. Recovering it automatically from ordinary Python is hard, and a long-term goal rather than today’s reality. Optimization. Turn naive code into strong execution plans: vectorization, register and shared-memory usage, barriers and atomics, cooperative threading, dead-buffer and redundant-traffic elimination, dropping needless synchronization. Move low-level optimization off users and into the platform. Primitives. Cholesky, eigendecomposition, matmul, reductions, solver kernels. Each owned with its correctness, benchmarks, and regression tracking. Watching Genesis and the compiler together. Hunt for performance wins on both sides, in Genesis and in Quadrants itself. Propose API changes that cut duplication, improve readability, and reduce platform-specific special-casing. Less to maintain, more that simply works. The project as a product. Benchmark real workloads, track performance over time, catch regressions early. Stay close to users (Genesis first), find friction and missing abstractions, drive adoption, set direction. Who you are You reason about whole systems and have taste for where complexity should live. You measure before you optimize, and you reach for memory traffic and launch overhead before FLOPs. You have opinions about API design. You write tests and benchmarks as you go, not afterward. The ground that judgment stands on: GPU. What optimal looks like and why: access patterns, registers, shared memory, barriers, atomics, threading. CPU intuition a plus. Python & API taste. Idiomatic Python. A feel for what’s natural to Python users. APIs that free users rather than constrain them. Compilers. The path from authoring to kernels (IR, lowering, optimization), weighed against maintainability. And how you work: proactive and largely self-directed. You fetch context across the company instead of waiting for it. You’re comfortable talking to the engineers who use what you build, and at ease designing in the open for users you’ll never meet. Ready to grow into leading a small team (a couple of people, near term). What great looks like People adopt Quadrants from outside Genesis. Engineers write clearer code with less boilerplate. Kernels keep getting faster. Performance is tracked, not guessed. The architecture gets easier to extend, not harder. What we’re uncompromising about How you work is up to you. What matters is that your ownership grows over time: blind spots shrink, the parts you can vouch for expand, technical debt goes down, the core stays sound. That takes treating understanding as real work, not overhead. You read and challenge the codebase instead of just stacking features on it. You take nothing you did not write for granted. You watch the competition and what’s coming next, and you bring it in and ship it. Use AI agents if they help. They are productivity tools, not code owners. You are. Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

data.title: Genesis-World: Core Physics Engineer
data.description: What we're building Robots will learn in simulation before they hit the factory. Genesis-World is our bet on that future. Genesis-World is an open-source, general-purpose simulation platform for physical AI from Genesis AI . One unified multi-physics engine: rigid bodies, FEM, MPM, particles, cloth, fluids. A robot arm can pour water onto sand, grasp a deformable object, or cut a soft body, all in the same simulation. Nyx, our in-house renderer, may be the most promising renderer for robotics out there: real-time photo-realistic rendering, advanced features like depth of field, and state-of-the-art techniques never seen before. Sensors of every kind: cameras, lidar, IMU, contact forces, temperature, plus arguably the most advanced tactile simulation available ( paper ). And the engine keeps growing: we are developing internally the most comprehensive and fastest Incremental Potential Contact ( paper ) solver for deformable body dynamics we know of, soon to be open-sourced. It powers real business applications, from full-fledged box packaging with labelling machine and all, to wire harnessing and lab automation, without any physics hack or compromise. Everything is Python-first and runs anywhere. Kernels are written once, and Quadrants, our in-house JIT compiler, lowers them to CUDA, AMD ROCm, Apple Metal, Vulkan, x86, and ARM64. A single laptop or a datacenter. Massively batched GPU simulation for learning at scale, and complex non-batched scenes where CPU wins outright. This is at the core of Genesis AI's strategy . Evaluation is the bottleneck of scalable robotics: real hardware caps iteration at wall-clock time, but simulation turns it into a compute problem. Ours already runs two orders of magnitude faster than hardware (tens of thousands of episodes in half an hour instead of 200+ hours), while correlating with on-hardware rollouts at 89%. The north star: physical AI that improves at the speed of compute. The role You push the physics of Genesis-World forward. The mandate is clear: ship production-ready simulation capabilities that matter for the company's internal needs. Research applied end-to-end, from algorithm to merged, tested, documented code that real robot-learning pipelines depend on. Occasional groundbreaking research happens, notably through academic collaborations. But the core of the job is making the engine measurably better along five axes: Speed. Algorithms that are not only faster but also smart enough to spend compute only where it matters across both time and space: larger stable timesteps, selective fidelity (adaptive across scales or simply hand-set), structure-aware solvers. Completeness. No physics off limits: water, human animation, air flow, gravel, tendons, even body organs. Whatever the next use-case needs, the engine grows to cover it. Fidelity. More realistic models: contact, friction, deformation, energy, actuation, materials… Versatility. Extensible multi-physics without compromise on realism: all solvers in the scene coupled together at once, two-way and constraint-based. Write your own solver and it joins the scene like a native one, growing into an open solver ecosystem. Scalability. From workstation to factory scale, and one day, city scale: thousands of interacting entities, batched across environments, without losing physical soundness. Our ambition is to establish Genesis-World as the go-to simulator for physical AI, from companies and research labs to individuals. The problems waiting for you Every fidelity for every physics. The same physics at every point of the speed-accuracy spectrum, from heavily batched training with XPBD or VBD to final validation with IPC. Same scene, same API, pick your tradeoff. Invent physics level-of-detail (LOD). Rendering has had LOD for decades, physics is still waiting. Simulate at full fidelity what agents interact with and see, coarsely what they do not. Heterogeneous environments. Every parallel world can hold a completely different model: different bodies, joints, and collision geometries. Adaptive timesteps per island. Error-based control with Runge-Kutta Dopri5, and Time-of-Impact stepping during collision detection, as done in Jiminy. Couple everything, exactly. Efficient and accurate two-way constraint-based coupling between heterogeneous grey-box solvers, using state-of-the-art methods like ADMM. Owning every solver in the stack is what makes it possible. More scalable constraint solvers. Push rigid constraint solving beyond its current scalability ceiling ( reference ). Unify contact resolution. Hydro-elastic compliance, unilateral constraints, and sequential impulses in the same framework, ideally under one generic formulation. Closed kinematic loops without constraints. Handle loops intrinsically for numerical stability and speed, in the spirit of Kamino . Day to day: you write your physics in plain Python and Quadrants makes it fast on every backend. And you validate it the hard way: analytical closed forms, other engines, real-world data. Who you are You are a physicist and an engineer at once. You judge a method by whether it holds up in production at real scale, and you do not stop until it does. No blind spots: you relentlessly hunt down even the defect that looks insignificant, because it never is. A strong background in physics-based simulation, preferably related to robotics: RBD, FEM, MPM, SPH, IPC, XPBD, VBD, ABD, plus constrained optimization and numerical integration of stiff systems. A track record of shipping simulation code that others rely on, in an engine, in industry, or in a research codebase used beyond its authors. Solid HPC programming (CPU and/or GPU), and an instinct for what makes a numerical method fast in practice, beyond complexity classes. Rigor in validation: analytical closed forms, cross-engine consistency, real-world data. Bonus points: publications in simulation, graphics, or robotics venues (SIGGRAPH, ICRA, IROS, CoRL, RSS). data.title: Genesis-World: Core Simulation Engine Engineer
data.description: What we’re building Robots will learn in simulation before they hit the factory. Genesis-World is our bet on that future. Genesis-World is an open-source, general-purpose simulation platform for physical AI from Genesis AI . One unified multi-physics engine: rigid bodies, FEM, MPM, particles, cloth, fluids. A robot arm can pour water onto sand, grasp a deformable object, or cut a soft body, all in the same simulation. Nyx, our in-house renderer, may be the most promising renderer for robotics out there: real-time photo-realistic rendering, advanced features like depth of field, and state-of-the-art techniques never seen before. Sensors of every kind: cameras, lidar, IMU, contact forces, temperature, plus arguably the most advanced tactile simulation available ( paper ). And the engine keeps growing: we are developing internally the most comprehensive and fastest Incremental Potential Contact ( paper ) solver for deformable body dynamics we know of, soon to be open-sourced. It powers real business applications, from full-fledged box packaging with labelling machine and all, to wire harnessing and lab automation, without any physics hack or compromise. Everything is Python-first and runs anywhere. Kernels are written once, and Quadrants, our in-house JIT compiler, lowers them to CUDA, AMD ROCm, Apple Metal, Vulkan, x86, and ARM64. A single laptop or a datacenter. Massively batched GPU simulation for learning at scale, and complex non-batched scenes where CPU wins outright. This is at the core of Genesis AI’s strategy . Evaluation is the bottleneck of scalable robotics: real hardware caps iteration at wall-clock time, but simulation turns it into a compute problem. Ours already runs two orders of magnitude faster than hardware (tens of thousands of episodes in half an hour instead of 200+ hours), while correlating with on-hardware rollouts at 89%. The north star: physical AI that improves at the speed of compute. The role Simulation is still a hard sell in robotics. Outside a few success stories, like reinforcement learning for locomotion, most teams skip it, and friction is a big part of why: painful to use, painful to debug. We live that pain ourselves: debugging a failing experiment during policy evaluation takes 30 minutes, and there is no way to automatically generate a standalone reproduction script. That blocks adoption, even internally. Your job is to kill that friction. You build the software engineering backbone of Genesis-World: everything that makes a large, fast-moving simulation codebase reliable, maintainable, frictionless. And it all ships in the open. Every hour of pain you remove, you remove for every roboticist who comes after you. You join as core maintainer of Genesis-World, with shared stewardship of the whole platform from day one. Our physics team develops the algorithms, but just as importantly, you work to make everything around them excellent: infrastructure, tooling, APIs, architecture. The problems waiting for you Make testing of a JIT-compiled engine scalable. Running our full suite is already taking hours because the ratio between compile time and runtime can be as bad as x10. Getting rid of this bottleneck is a serious challenge that will require a joint effort from the Genesis-World and the compiler teams. Make any bug reproducible. Dump and reload simulations bit-exactly, across machines, across backends, even when a single timestep of a batched simulation can already max out VRAM. Turn any failing run into a standalone reproduction script, automatically. Make autodiff first-class. Genesis-World is differentiable today, but partially: memory-hungry, slower than it could be, and hard to maintain due to manual operation recording. The project spans the engine and the compiler: you drive the requirements on Quadrants and iterate in a tight loop with the compiler team until the integration is solid. Edit scenes at frozen time. See the scene, move entities and robots around, iterate on layout, all without building the scene or compiling the engine. Authoring today means a full build cycle. Make it instant. Make the simulator extensible. First-class plugins for physics solvers and interactive viewer backends, including Nyx. Sensors already work this way. Generalize it, and Genesis-World becomes a platform others build on. Give robots real actuation. Motors and MIMO transmissions, cleanly abstracted at the interface between users and the physics engine. Make time a local variable. Today the clock and the timestep are global to the engine, which forbids whole classes of speedups: environments cannot step independently, the timestep cannot adapt to the state, and individual solvers cannot advance at their own rate. Free the clock down to the sub-scene level and let the simulation fly. Make scenes come alive. Events triggered by physics: press the button and the microwave door pops open, squeeze the trigger and the drill spins. Keep the core sharp. Refactoring legacy subsystems, stronger typing, consistent coding style, less Python overhead on hot paths, full scene serialization, telemetry and replay. Beyond the code: you review issues and pull requests with the core team, answer questions from users and contributors, and can join the push on adoption. Who you are You care about the engineer using what you build as much as the thing itself. A slow test, a cryptic error, a manual step: you see it, you go after the root cause, and you remove it for everyone. You have opinions about API design. You are comfortable with physics and robotics: the right design choices take a working picture of what a simulator like Genesis-World does, how it works, and how it is used, a picture you can partly build on the job. Strong Python engineering on large codebases: architecture, refactoring, typing, packaging, performance profiling (py-spy, Nsight, Xcode Instruments, RenderDoc). Developer tooling, test infrastructure, or CI at scale. Enough fluency with JIT compilation, code generation, or GPU computing stacks to reason about compilation caching, kernel dispatch, and startup cost. You will work closely with Quadrants. At ease debugging across the full platform matrix: Windows, Linux, and macOS, on x86 and arm64, over CUDA, AMD, and Apple Metal (and possibly Intel XPU via Vulkan soon) Open-source reflexes: triaging issues, reviewing external pull requests, communicating with a community. Bonus points: experience with other robotics simulators (Drake, MuJoCo, Newton, Isaac, RaiSim, Jiminy, Brax). PyTorch, our user-facing interface. Other JIT compilers such as Triton, JAX, or Numba. 3D tooling and interactive editors (Maya, Blender, Houdini). Serialization formats (USD, glTF, MJCF/URDF). C++, CUDA, or Metal. Developer relations or community work. Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

data.title: General Counsel at amo
data.description: amo is a Paris-based consumer social company. We want to build Europe's most ambitious consumer company. Our apps Bump and Sugar are used by millions of people all over the globe. Location sits at the heart of one of our current products, and privacy, trust and safety are part of how we build, not an afterthought. We're scaling fast, and this comes with legal implications. We want them handled in a way that speeds the business up. The role: We're hiring our first General Counsel to own amo's legal function end to end. This is a business role, not a support function: you'll work directly with the cofounders, join discussions from the start and work with every team, from Product and Distribution to People, Engineering and Finance. You'll draft, negotiate and advise yourself on the topics that matter most. For everything else, you'll build and run a network of local counsel, with the right firm for each topic and each market, and turn their advice into clear decisions for the team. How we think about legal: At amo, legal starts from the product, to serve our users. We're not looking for someone who applies the rules by the book, but for someone who understands what we're building and why, and finds the legal approach that makes sense for it. You'll be judged on what you enable, not on how many memos you write. Product and users first: you join discussions early and work with the team toward the same goal: making projects to life, fast and safe. Pragmatic on risk: you know which rules are non-negotiable, where there is room for judgement, and how much risk is worth taking for the business. You give a recommendation, not a list of risks. Built for scale: you set up the contracts, policies and processes that enable our growth. What you'll own: You'll cover every legal question that comes with scaling a consumer app across markets, working with the right local counsel on each topic: Corporate: general corporate, group structure as we expand internationally, BSPCE plans and employee liquidity operations. Employment: French labour law across the employee lifecycle, from contracts, immigration and internal rules to terminations. Trademarks and IP: our global trademark portfolio: filing strategy, oppositions, watch services and disputes. Patents and content licensing as they come. Compliance and data protection: GDPR, protection of minors, DSA, app store policies, and more. Regulator and law enforcement requests. Commercial contracts: vendors and SaaS, partnerships, creator and influencer agreements, advertising, data processing agreements. Templates and a self-serve process so teams can move autonomously. Litigation: pre-litigation and litigation across jurisdictions, with outside counsel. Clear risk assessments and options for the cofounders. M&A: acquisitions and strategic transactions when the time comes, including due diligence, structuring and integration. What success looks like: Teams ship features, sign deals and expand without waiting on legal. The cofounders spend far less time on legal: topics get tracked, briefed and closed without one of them driving each one, and nothing is discovered late. The right local counsel is in place for each topic and market, on a budget we control. What we're looking for: Startup and scaleup experience, at our stage and beyond. 7+ years of legal experience, including a senior in-house role (General Counsel, Deputy GC or Head of Legal) at a tech company. You've lived the stage we're at international expansion, fast growth. Expert in French and EU law. French legal training, with deep knowledge of French corporate and employment law, GDPR and EU digital regulation. Admission to the bar (CAPA) is a plus. Global outlook. data.title: Senior Quantum Optics Scientist - Spin-Based Quantum Systems
data.description: - About Quandela: Quandela is a European deeptech scale-up developing modular, scalable and energy-efficient photonic and spin-optical quantum computers, accessible through the cloud and on-premises. With over 140 employees, we develop our own hardware and software stack, from semiconductor quantum emitters and photonic processors to quantum control systems and algorithms. Our ambition is to build large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computers, combining quantum dot technologies, scalable spin-photon interfaces and distributed entanglement within future Spin-Optical Quantum Computing (SPOQC) architectures. - About this position: You will join Quandela's Semiconductor Optics Team, bringing together expertise in quantum optics, spin physics, semiconductor technologies and quantum information. Your focus will be to develop and validate photon-mediated spin-spin entanglement protocols , improve spin coherence and operation fidelity, and advance optical control techniques for future hybrid quantum computing architectures. We are looking for an experienced experimental scientist who can independently drive complex experimental activities, shape technical directions and translate scientific results into reliable technological building blocks , working closely with our research and engineering teams. With several experimental building blocks still under development, you'll have room to shape technical choices, tackle open scientific challenges and directly influence our technology roadmap. - What you'll do: Spin-based quantum experiments Design, develop and optimize optical experiments involving spin-photon sources. Implement optical control schemes for spin initialization, readout and manipulation. Characterize spin coherence, operation fidelity and entanglement quality. Scientific and experimental ownership Independently drive experimental investigations, from design to validation. Structure and prioritize scientific activities, milestones and technical challenges. Troubleshoot complex experimental systems and propose technical improvements. Share expertise and support less experienced colleagues when relevant. Technology development and integration Develop and validate photon-mediated spin-spin entanglement protocols. Collaborate with theory, electronics and semiconductor technology teams. Improve experimental robustness, reproducibility and system performance. Translate scientific results into demonstrators and technological building blocks for future multi-spin architectures. - How You Will Grow: During your first 3 months You will become familiar with Quandela's experimental platforms and ongoing demonstrators, contributing your expertise to current technical challenges. Within 6 months You will drive dedicated experimental workstreams, contribute to key technical decisions and strengthen theory-to-experiment feedback loops. Within 1 year You will help shape the team's experimental direction, advance distributed entanglement demonstrations and contribute to future spin-based architectures. Requirements - What we're looking for We are looking for an experienced experimental researcher combining strong scientific expertise, technical autonomy and the ability to drive complex research activities. Must-have PhD in Spin Physics, Quantum Optics or a related field. Hands-on experience with spin-based quantum systems (control, readout or coherence measurements). Proven autonomy in designing, optimizing and troubleshooting complex quantum experiments. Strong understanding of quantum optics, spin coherence and experimental measurement techniques. Ability to lead scientific activities and make independent technical decisions. Comfortable collaborating across experimental, theory and engineering teams Important, but you can grow here Photon-mediated entanglement protocols and multi-spin architectures. Semiconductor quantum emitters, quantum dots and spin-photon interfaces. Advanced optical control, cryogenic platforms and fast electronics. Experimental qualification, system integration and technology transfer. Bonus points Experience bridging academic research and industrial R&D. Experience coordinating scientific projects or mentoring researchers. - Career Stage & Team Contribution: We primarily target candidates with a PhD and 4+ years of postdoctoral or equivalent R&D experience , combining scientific expertise with strong experimental autonomy. Researchers completing a substantial postdoc are also welcome if they demonstrate scientific maturity, technical ownership and readiness for broader responsibilities. People management experience is not required. What matters is your ability to drive scientific activities, tackle complex technical challenges and share your expertise with the team. Benefits Profit-sharing and a company savings plan. Public transport subscription covered at 50%. Annual sustainable mobility bonus for eco-friendly transport (e-bike, electric car). Fully covered health insurance (Alan). Referral program (€1,000 for a junior and €2,000 for an experienced candidate). Access to a nursery via choisir-ma-creche or contribution to childcare expenses. Subsidy for gym membership and sports activities (Gymlib). Meal subsidies (Swile). Localisation of the position : Based at the IPVF campus in Palaiseau, within the Paris-Saclay research ecosystem. Process: Talent Acquisition Interview (30–45 min) Hiring Manager Interview (45–60 min) Technical discussion and presentation of previous research work Meeting with the team and scientific discussion Reference checks Offer - Beyond That At Quandela, you'll work on challenging scientific questions while helping turn experimental advances into technologies for future quantum computers. Our spin-based platforms are still evolving, leaving room to explore new approaches, influence technical directions and take real ownership of experimental challenges. If you're excited by the idea of combining ambitious quantum research with tangible technological impact, we'd love to hear from you, even if your background doesn't match every requirement. data.title: GPU Engineer
data.description: About Kog At Kog, we're building real-time LLM inference for AI agents. Coding agents execute sequences of tasks where each step depends on the model's previous response. The faster the model generates tokens, the faster these agents can reason, code, and act. Our approach is to co-design model architecture, the inference engine, and low-level GPU kernels to minimize generation latency on standard NVIDIA and AMD datacenter GPUs. We've developed several technologies to make this possible: Monokernel: a persistent GPU program that keeps the entire token generation loop on the GPU, avoiding CPU handoffs. KCCL: our custom inter-GPU communication layer, designed to minimize latency. Delayed Tensor Parallelism (DTP): a model architecture that overlaps communication with computation and weight loading. Laneformer 2B: our code-generation model demonstrating this co-design approach. Our engineers work directly with GPU hardware, using CUDA, PTX, HIP, and CDNA ISA to optimize execution. Implementing and optimizing a new AI model for a specific GPU architecture can take months of manual engineering. Meanwhile, new models are constantly being released. Our goal is to use AI agents to implement and optimize the models we choose on the GPUs we choose, in a fraction of the time required today. These agents will build on the GPU optimizations and hardware insights our team has developed. They'll explore optimization strategies, generate and modify kernels, verify correctness, benchmark performance on real hardware, and iterate based on the results. We want to make model porting and GPU optimization much faster and repeatable, allowing Kog to keep pace with the latest AI models rather than spending months adapting each one manually. This is a major engineering direction we're now developing, and you'll help shape it. Learn more at https://blog.kog.ai . What you'll work on You'll join our GPU engineering team to tackle challenging performance problems and help build the internal agents that will accelerate this work. Develop and optimize GPU kernels using C++, CUDA, HIP, and low-level instructions. Investigate GPU architecture, memory access, synchronization, and execution bottlenecks. Profile and benchmark workloads to identify and validate performance improvements. Optimize inference operations and communication across multiple GPUs. Implement and optimize new AI models on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs. Help build AI agents for GPU engineering , enabling automated code optimization, correctness testing, benchmarking, and iterative improvements. Take ownership of technical decisions and their implementation. What we're looking for We're looking for an experienced GPU Engineer who can contribute quickly and independently to complex performance problems. Strong hands-on experience developing and optimizing GPU kernels, ideally using CUDA C++ or HIP/ROCm. Deep understanding of GPU architecture, memory hierarchy, parallel execution, and performance bottlenecks. Strong C++ skills and experience profiling and benchmarking GPU workloads. Proven ownership of challenging technical projects, from implementation to measured results. Interest in developing AI agents and tools to accelerate GPU engineering. Experience with PTX, CDNA ISA, multi-GPU systems, low-latency inference, or GPU performance portability is particularly valuable. A PhD in HPC, computer science, or a related field is a plus when backed by substantial engineering work. Previous experience building AI agents is not required. Location and availability Candidates must already be based in Paris or elsewhere in Île-de-France. We are not considering relocation from other regions or countries for this position. We're looking for someone who can join the team quickly. Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

data.description: About Pangea Propulsion: We are a company dedicated to developing advanced propulsion systems for the space industry based on three key principles: high efficiency, sustainability, and reusability. We are revolutionizing the space industry with ground-breaking innovations that allow us to offer the best performance to cost propulsion systems. Our goal is to be the propulsion provider for the next generation of spacecraft, which is essential to meet demands and compete in the booming space market of the next decade. We are a passionate, multicultural, and multidisciplinary team pushing the boundaries of what is possible in space propulsion technology. We have already made history by successfully testing the world's first 3D-printed Methalox Aerospike engine, marking a significant milestone for the space industry. We are looking for talented professionals to join our international teams in Barcelona and Toulouse. We want to be a key player in improving diversity in the Aerospace sector as, in Pangea, we believe that diversity (gender, age, race, sexual orientation, beliefs, disability, culture, etc.) is a key to success. Within Pangea, everyone can grow with the same opportunities. We encourage you to apply. Individually we are different, but together we are an amazing team! We are looking for a CFD Workflow Automation Intern for a 6-month internship in Toulouse. About the role: We are seeking a highly skilled intern with a strong programming background and an interest in engineering simulation to help automate repetitive CFD activities across the Turbomachinery Fluidic Design Team and the Fluidic Analysis Team. The role will focus on developing robust, reusable workflows for meshing, simulation setup and launching, data extraction, post-processing, and standardized reporting, with particular emphasis on Cadence and Ansys Fluent environments. The internship is intended to reduce manual effort, improve repeatability, and shorten analysis turnaround time across the Fluidics Department. The intern will work with engineers from both teams to identify high-value automation opportunities, translate existing engineering practices into scripts and workflows, and validate the resulting tools on representative analysis cases. Prior expertise in Cadence or Ansys Fluent is not required; strong programming ability and a willingness to learn the relevant engineering applications are more important. Key Responsibilities: • Develop scripts and utilities to automate CFD meshing, simulation setup, job launching, monitoring, and post-processing activities. • Automate recurring workflows in Cadence and Ansys Fluent, using the scripting and interface capabilities available within those environments. • Create reusable tools for data extraction, visualization, comparison, and standardized reporting of CFD results. • Work with the Turbomachinery Fluidic Design Team to streamline the design-analysis iteration loop, including comparison of CFD results with design intent. • Work with the Fluidic Analysis Team to identify repetitive analysis tasks and convert them into reliable, maintainable automated processes. • Define input requirements, verification checks, error handling, and user documentation so that the developed tools can be adopted by different engineers. • Validate automated workflows against existing manual processes and document accuracy, repeatability, limitations, and expected time savings. • Present progress and results to the participating teams and incorporate user feedback into successive tool improvements. What you need to be successful: • Final-year student or recent graduate in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical field. • Strong programming skills, preferably in Python; experience with additional scripting languages is an advantage. • Understanding of software development fundamentals, including modular code, version control, testing, debugging, and documentation. • Ability to analyse an existing manual workflow, identify repetitive steps, and translate the process into a structured automation solution. • Interest in CFD, numerical simulation, engineering data processing, or scientific computing. Previous application-specific experience is not mandatory. • Fluency in written and spoken English. Soft Skills: • Analytical and methodical approach to problem solving. • Proactive mindset and willingness to take ownership of a defined work package. • Clear communication and ability to gather requirements from engineers in different teams. • Attention to detail, with a focus on reliability, traceability, and usability. • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively in a multicultural, multidisciplinary environment. Other useful skills: • Experience with engineering or scientific Python and Matlab libraries for data processing and visualization. • Familiarity with Linux, command-line tools, batch processing, high-performance computing, or job schedulers. • Exposure to APIs, graphical user interfaces, dashboards, or automated report generation. • Familiarity with Git or another version-control system. • Previous exposure to Cadence, Ansys Fluent, CFD meshing, or simulation postprocessing is beneficial but not required. • Basic knowledge of fluid dynamics or numerical methods is an advantage. Supervision and collaboration: The intern will be supervised by a designated engineer and will collaborate with representatives of both the Turbomachinery Fluidic Design Team and the Fluidic Analysis Team. The assignment will be managed as a shared departmental initiative, with priorities defined according to the automation needs and potential impact identified by the participating teams.
